title: Israel's Iron Beam laser may have made its first combat interception, of a Hezbollah drone, in footage of 2 March 2026; the military said on 12 March that Iron Beam had not been used
summary: Footage of 2 March 2026 may show Israel's Iron Beam laser downing a Hezbollah drone; the military said on 12 March that Iron Beam had not been used, and only the OECD entry calls the laser AI.
account: The OECD AI Incidents entry, dated 28 February 2026, says that Israel “deployed its AI-powered Iron Beam laser defense system for the first time in combat to intercept Hezbollah missile barrages”. It separately bundles a Hankyoreh item (dated 10 October 2023) on Hamas rockets penetrating Iron Dome. Metro, Economic Times, MoneyControl's second item, Hankyoreh and others among the Monitor's 20 listed sources are syndications or explainers. No cited source describes Iron Beam as an AI system. The only other mention of AI is Rafael's chief executive framing machine learning as a future capability (Breaking Defense, 22 October 2025). That piece is not among the sources. The only confirmed combat use of a laser is aggregate and earlier. A lower-powered, shorter-range variant shot down some 35 drones from Lebanon in 2024 (Times of Israel/AFP). The Ministry of Defense announced it in May 2025 (The Jerusalem Post). The ministry said that no Iron Beam components were involved (Wikipedia). The Times of Israel reports the Defense Ministry's handover of the first operational system on 28 December 2025, after tests against rockets, mortars and drones. The Iron Beam claim rests on social-media footage from Monday 2 March 2026, a later date than the Monitor's. Ynet (Yair Kraus) reports that the footage “appeared to show the first operational use” of the system. It was delivered to the Israeli Air Force in late December 2025. Hezbollah fired rockets and drones from Lebanon after the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader, with one drone intercepted near Shlomi. The Jerusalem Post (Seth Frantzman, 2 March 2026) says that the circulated video “did not show lasers intercepting rockets”. TimesNow (2 March 2026) says that whether this was Iron Beam's first combat use “awaits official confirmation”. Army Recognition (3 March 2026) says that officials “have not formally confirmed the specific engagements” and that no authoritative combat log names the system. Moneycontrol (3 March 2026) sources its “first-ever use” to an “Israel War Room” social-media video. The Conversation (4 March 2026) calls the reports unconfirmed. The Jerusalem Post reported on 12 March 2026 that the Israel Defense Forces said that Iron Beam had not been used and was not ready for regular use in the war. Times of Israel/AFP (16 March 2026) reports that the military “has so far refused to comment on its use during the ongoing war”. Times of Israel (Stav Levaton, 27 March 2026) reports that “military officials said it has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. On 1 May 2026 the Israel Air Force said that the system saw less use because it needs 14 batteries for a significant impact. Times of Israel (Emanuel Fabian, 30 June 2026) reports that the one deployed system “has seen limited use and has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. A senior officer called its coverage partial. A senior defense official told Ynetnews on 9 August 2026 that the one system delivered in December 2025 was still not operational.
purpose: Iron Beam is a high-energy laser built to intercept rockets, mortars and drones at short range. It is a low-cost complement to Iron Dome, David's Sling and Arrow. Interception of Hezbollah projectiles is its stated purpose.
system: Iron Beam ('Or Eitan') 100 kW-class high-energy laser air-defense system by Rafael Advanced Defense Systems, with beam director and electro-optical targeting; the Monitor calls it 'AI-enabled', which no cited source supports
developer: Rafael Advanced Defense Systems with the Israel Ministry of Defense (Lockheed Martin collaboration for the US market, per Wikipedia)
deployer: Israeli Air Force air-defense array; first operational system delivered 28 December 2025
location: Northern Israel near the Lebanese border (Shlomi area reported), Israel
segment: Directed-energy interception of rockets, mortars and drones
taxonomy_note: An intercepted drone or rockets are read as a physically harmful incident averted; no defense type exists.

ratings.reason: Ynet reports that one drone was intercepted and no injuries occurred in the 2 March 2026 launches. No official source attributes any interception to Iron Beam.

The Israel Defense Forces said on 12 March 2026 that Iron Beam had not been used in the war. Officials later described limited use and partial coverage, and a senior defense official said on 9 August 2026 that the one delivered system was still not operational.

ai_role.statement: No cited source describes Iron Beam as an AI or machine-learning system. Those sources are Ynet, JPost, Army Recognition, TimesNow, The Conversation and Moneycontrol. They also include Times of Israel 28 December 2025, 16 Mar, 27 Mar and 30 June 2026, and Wikipedia. They describe a high-power laser with a beam director and electro-optical targeting. The Monitor's “AI-enabled” label is its own. Rafael's CEO described machine learning as a future capability (Breaking Defense, 22 October 2025). The IDF has not confirmed the engagement itself, so neither an AI role nor a contribution can be assessed.

fields.account: The OECD AI Incidents entry, dated 28 February 2026, says that Israel “deployed its AI-powered Iron Beam laser defense system for the first time in combat to intercept Hezbollah missile barrages”. It separately bundles a Hankyoreh item (dated 10 October 2023) on Hamas rockets penetrating Iron Dome. Metro, Economic Times, MoneyControl's second item, Hankyoreh and others among the Monitor's 20 listed sources are syndications or explainers. No cited source describes Iron Beam as an AI system. The only other mention of AI is Rafael's chief executive framing machine learning as a future capability (Breaking Defense, 22 October 2025). That piece is not among the sources. The only confirmed combat use of a laser is aggregate and earlier. A lower-powered, shorter-range variant shot down some 35 drones from Lebanon in 2024 (Times of Israel/AFP). The Ministry of Defense announced it in May 2025 (The Jerusalem Post). The ministry said that no Iron Beam components were involved (Wikipedia). The Times of Israel reports the Defense Ministry's handover of the first operational system on 28 December 2025, after tests against rockets, mortars and drones. The Iron Beam claim rests on social-media footage from Monday 2 March 2026, a later date than the Monitor's. Ynet (Yair Kraus) reports that the footage “appeared to show the first operational use” of the system. It was delivered to the Israeli Air Force in late December 2025. Hezbollah fired rockets and drones from Lebanon after the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader, with one drone intercepted near Shlomi. The Jerusalem Post (Seth Frantzman, 2 March 2026) says that the circulated video “did not show lasers intercepting rockets”. TimesNow (2 March 2026) says that whether this was Iron Beam's first combat use “awaits official confirmation”. Army Recognition (3 March 2026) says that officials “have not formally confirmed the specific engagements” and that no authoritative combat log names the system. Moneycontrol (3 March 2026) sources its “first-ever use” to an “Israel War Room” social-media video. The Conversation (4 March 2026) calls the reports unconfirmed. The Jerusalem Post reported on 12 March 2026 that the Israel Defense Forces said that Iron Beam had not been used and was not ready for regular use in the war. Times of Israel/AFP (16 March 2026) reports that the military “has so far refused to comment on its use during the ongoing war”. Times of Israel (Stav Levaton, 27 March 2026) reports that “military officials said it has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. On 1 May 2026 the Israel Air Force said that the system saw less use because it needs 14 batteries for a significant impact. Times of Israel (Emanuel Fabian, 30 June 2026) reports that the one deployed system “has seen limited use and has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. A senior officer called its coverage partial. A senior defense official told Ynetnews on 9 August 2026 that the one system delivered in December 2025 was still not operational.

chronology_source.title: AI-Enabled Iron Beam and Iron Dome Systems Deployed in Israeli Defense

display.answer: The interception claim traces to a social-media video of 2 March 2026, which Ynet, The Jerusalem Post, Times Now, Army Recognition, Moneycontrol and The Conversation report, and the Monitor relays it with its own AI label. The later reports by The Jerusalem Post, The Times of Israel and Ynetnews rest on statements by the military, the Israel Air Force and a senior defense official.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: Footage of 2 March 2026 may show Israel's Iron Beam laser downing a Hezbollah drone; the military said on 12 March that Iron Beam had not been used, and only the OECD entry calls the laser AI.
fields.account: The OECD AI Incidents entry, dated 28 February 2026, says that Israel “deployed its AI-powered Iron Beam laser defense system for the first time in combat to intercept Hezbollah missile barrages”. It separately bundles a Hankyoreh item (dated 10 October 2023) on Hamas rockets penetrating Iron Dome. Metro, Economic Times, MoneyControl's second item, Hankyoreh and others among the Monitor's 20 listed sources are syndications or explainers. No cited source describes Iron Beam as an AI system. The only other mention of AI is Rafael's chief executive framing machine learning as a future capability (Breaking Defense, 22 October 2025). That piece is not among the sources. The only confirmed combat use of a laser is aggregate and earlier. A lower-powered, shorter-range variant shot down some 35 drones from Lebanon in 2024 (Times of Israel/AFP). The Ministry of Defense announced it in May 2025 (The Jerusalem Post). The ministry said that no Iron Beam components were involved (Wikipedia). The Times of Israel reports the Defense Ministry's handover of the first operational system on 28 December 2025, after tests against rockets, mortars and drones. The Iron Beam claim rests on social-media footage from Monday 2 March 2026, a later date than the Monitor's. Ynet (Yair Kraus) reports that the footage “appeared to show the first operational use” of the system. It was delivered to the Israeli Air Force in late December 2025. Hezbollah fired rockets and drones from Lebanon after the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader, with one drone intercepted near Shlomi. The Jerusalem Post (Seth Frantzman, 2 March 2026) says that the circulated video “did not show lasers intercepting rockets”. TimesNow (2 March 2026) says that whether this was Iron Beam's first combat use “awaits official confirmation”. Army Recognition (3 March 2026) says that officials “have not formally confirmed the specific engagements” and that no authoritative combat log names the system. Moneycontrol (3 March 2026) sources its “first-ever use” to an “Israel War Room” social-media video. The Conversation (4 March 2026) calls the reports unconfirmed. The Jerusalem Post reported on 12 March 2026 that the Israel Defense Forces said that Iron Beam had not been used and was not ready for regular use in the war. Times of Israel/AFP (16 March 2026) reports that the military “has so far refused to comment on its use during the ongoing war”. Times of Israel (Stav Levaton, 27 March 2026) reports that “military officials said it has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. On 1 May 2026 the Israel Air Force said that the system saw less use because it needs 14 batteries for a significant impact. Times of Israel (Emanuel Fabian, 30 June 2026) reports that the one deployed system “has seen limited use and has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. A senior officer called its coverage partial. A senior defense official told Ynetnews on 9 August 2026 that the one system delivered in December 2025 was still not operational.

produced_by: A ground-based high-energy laser that holds its beam on a short-range target within line of sight until it is destroyed. JPost describes the terrain, weather and dwell-time limits
Integration into the Israeli Air Force's layered air-defense array as a complement to Iron Dome
must_hold: IDF confirmation that Iron Beam, not Iron Dome, other interceptors or counter-UAS effects, made the 2 March 2026 interception
Line of sight and clear weather. A senior officer said in May 2026 that the system's coverage is partial and that at least 14 batteries are sought

echoes.setting: 2024 conflict with Hezbollah, northern Israel: a lower-powered, shorter-range laser variant shot down some 35 drones (Times of Israel/AFP), announced by the Ministry of Defense in May 2025 (JPost); the MoD said no Iron Beam components were involved (Wikipedia)
echoes.model_version: lower-powered variant (Lite Beam or Iron Beam-M, per Wikipedia's account of Israeli media)
